title: Emergent Polar Order at Low Temperatures Revealed by Atomic-Resolution Cryogenic Electron Microscopy
content: In condensed matter systems, abundant symmetry breaking phases emerge below room temperature, spanning superconductivity [1], metal-insulator transition [2], and electronic crystallization [3]. Polar order is the order parameter in ferroelectrics, which usually originates from atomic shifts that break inversion symmetry [4]. The behaviour of polar order at low temperature has been rarely explored [5, 6] because polar order typically appears far above room temperature in most ferroelectrics, leading to a focus on high-temperature behaviour. Here, we show two cases where cryogenic electron microscopy reveals novel phenomena associated with polar order.
